summary.short: Amends California Penal Code §§ 311–311.12 so child sexual abuse material and obscenity offenses also cover digitally altered or AI-generated depictions of what appears to be a person under 18; adds an AI definition. Operative only if SB 1381 is enacted and takes effect on or before January 1, 2025.
summary.long: Adds legislative findings on AI-generated child sexual abuse material (Sec. 1) and amends Penal Code §§ 311, 311.2, 311.11 and 311.12. Section 311 adds a definition of artificial intelligence. Section 311.2 covers matter containing digitally altered or AI-generated content that depicts, or appears to depict, a person under 18 in sexual conduct: subdivision (b) makes commercial sending, distribution or exhibition of obscene matter a felony (two, three or six years in state prison, a fine up to $100,000, or both); subdivision (c) covers distribution to adults (misdemeanor, up to one year in county jail, fine up to $2,000, or state prison; felony after a prior conviction); subdivision (d) covers distribution to persons under 18 (felony). Section 311.11 penalizes possession or control of such matter (felony; fine up to $2,500), with enhanced penalties for prior convictions and listed aggravating factors. Section 311.12 adds a fine up to $2,000 for offenses involving government-owned computers or property. Exemptions cover law enforcement, certain medical, scientific or educational activities, and emancipated minors (§ 311.2(e)–(f)). Section 7 makes the act operative only if SB 1381 (2023–24) is enacted and takes effect on or before January 1, 2025.

notes: The document reproduces amended sections in full without underline or strike marking, so changed text cannot be separated from unchanged text; relations describe the four amended Penal Code sections. Sec. 7 makes the whole act conditional on SB 1381. Sec. 3 § 311.2(b) reads 'contains a digitally altered or artificial-intelligence-generated depiction what appears to be', apparently missing 'of'. Sec. 1 findings are not operative provisions. Sec. 2 § 311(b) defines 'Artificial intelligence' without limiting it to generative systems.

obligations.summary: Counties must deposit revenue from fines collected under Penal Code § 311.12 into a county fund and allocate it one-third each to sexual assault investigator training, to shelters and services for trafficking victims, and to multidisciplinary teams; a county may transfer allocations to another county.
